keyword: silver alongside stocks and bonds diversification guide
angle: How to size a silver allocation alongside stocks and bonds in 2026, using Silver Institute supply/demand data, Oxford Economics allocation research, and current correlation dynamics.
secondary_kw: silver vs stocks and bonds correlation

stats.claim: Oxford Economics research commissioned by the Silver Institute concludes an optimal multi-asset portfolio should include a 4-6% allocation to silver, versus the roughly 0.2% most investors currently hold.

The Silver Institute forecasts a sixth consecutive global silver market deficit in 2026 of roughly 46.3 million ounces, widening from 40.3 Moz in 2025 as investment demand absorbs metal left by industry.
Physical silver investment demand is forecast to rise 18% in 2026 to its highest level since 2022, driven largely by a projected 57% rebound in US retail demand.
Silver industrial fabrication is forecast to slip 2% in 2026 to a four-year low near 650 million ounces as photovoltaic thrifting offsets growth from AI data centers and autos.

J.P. Morgan Global Research projects silver will average $81/oz in 2026, more than double its 2025 average, reinforcing the case for a strategic precious metals sleeve alongside equities and bonds. Silver was $57.50/oz on 2026-06-27.

Gold's historical correlation to the S&P 500 has typically ranged from roughly -0.1 to 0.2, illustrating why precious metals add diversification when stock/bond correlations turn positive (as they have since 2021).
Silver returned roughly 145% in 2025 versus gold's 64%, outperforming the S&P 500 by a wide margin and demonstrating silver's high-beta role within a metals allocation.
